title: Signal decomposition lab notes — session 2
content:
Session objective:
- Break down noisy latency signals observed during last canary (2026-01-12).
- Propose compact metric set + trace anchors for fast triage and low query cost.

Executive notes (short):
- Root cause candidates: cross-tenant KV eviction, model variant increase in seq len distribution, tiny autoscale gaps. Traces point to increased backend cpu queue time for ~12% of requests.
- Goal: define 6–8 signals that give >90% diagnostic coverage for the above classes while keeping query cost under budget.

Metric definitions (proposed canonical list):
1) request.count (per-route, per-tenant): count of top-level inference requests.
   - granularity: 1m/1h
   - labels: route, model_version, tenant_id, region, deployment_tier
2) latency.ttfb_ms (time-to-first-token): measured at gateway entry to first token emitted by runtime.
   - quantiles: p50,p90,p99
3) latency.total_token_ms_per_token (per-token generation time excluding network): total runtime token time / tokens generated.
   - why: normalizes across long responses, surfaces model perf regression.
4) kvcache.warmth_ratio (prefix_warm_requests / requests) per-tenant/model-version
   - helps detect cold-cache regressions; important for dedicated/private customers
5) backend.cpu_queue_ms (time waiting for executor scheduling on host)
   - aggregated per-pool and per-machine-type
6) autoscale.backoff_events.count (times scaling decision delayed due to policy limits)
7) routing.fanout_multiplier (average fanout for multi-model requests)
8) error.rate_alarm (>=5xx or structured internal_error)

Naming conventions: use dot.delimited names; avoid verbs in metric name; include stable label set. Metric contracts should include: description, unit, cardinality guidance, expected pre-rollout baseline, and SLO relevance.

Trace design and anchors:
- Span taxonomy: gateway -> router -> model-runtime -> kv-store -> network-proxy (if present).
- Key span attributes to include: trace_id, request_id, tenant_id, route, model_version, seq_len, kv_hit (bool), cpu_wait_ms, queue_depth, host_id. Keep attr count limited to avoid cardinality explosion.
- Sampling policy: severity-weighted adaptive sampling. Always sample traces where backend.cpu_queue_ms > 50ms OR latency.total_token_ms_per_token > baseline*1.4. For general traffic, deterministic sampling at 0.05% with reservoir for recent failures.
- Trace anchors for rollouts: add span annotation rollout_tag and canary_bucket; annotate model_version_variant and quantization_profile. That lets us pivot dashboard panels by variant quickly.

Dashboard composition notes (cost-aware):
- Panel set A (operator quickcard): 6 panels, query window 15m, refresh 30s. Purpose: fast triage in slack/ops. Panels: overall request.count, p99 ttfb, kvcache.warmth_ratio, backend.cpu_queue_ms p99, error.rate_alarm, autoscale.backoff_events.
- Panel set B (deep investigation): 12 panels, window 24h, refresh 5m. Includes histograms for seq_len, token/time scatter, trace-sampled waterfall, tenant-weighted cost map.
- Query budgeting: cap deep queries to run only on demand; default dashboard should load in <2s for operators. Use pre-aggregated rollups for p90/p99 at 1m resolution.

Investigation playbook (operator flow):
1) Check operator quickcard. If p99 ttfb spike: jump to kvcache.warmth_ratio and backend.cpu_queue_ms.
2) If kvcache warm_ratio low for affected tenant → check recent model_version rollouts or tenant cache TTL changes (link to rollout audit).
3) If backend.cpu_queue_ms high across pool → open host-level heatmap, check autoscale.backoff_events. If backoff present, escalate SRE to inspect scaling policy logs.
4) If sample traces show model-runtime compute spikes correlated with seq_len → consider early mitigation: limit max tokens on canary route or rollback model variant.

Prototype experiments (short-term):
- Exp A: Create synthetic probe (lightweight request shape) to run every minute against canary route and record kvcache.warmth_ratio + ttfb. Purpose: detect cache churn within 10 minutes. (Ticket: JIRA-ENG-2581)
- Exp B: Enable severity-weighted trace reservoir for 6 hours during next canary and collect 5k traces for offline analysis.
- Exp C: Build per-tenant cheap summary (approx count sketch) for seq_len distribution to reduce trace reliance.

Dashboard UX decisions and micro-optimizations:
- Use compact sparkline rows for tenant lists + per-tenant delta bar to reduce vertical space.
- Default to grouped-by-route; allow quick toggle to group-by-tenant for customer-facing incidents.
- Annotate panels with quick-lookup links: trace search pre-filled, relevant PRs, canary rollout window.

Open questions / tradeoffs to resolve:
- Cardinality guardrails: which labels are allowed for high-cardinality metrics? Proposal: tenant_id allowed only on rollup metrics; host_id only on troubleshooting-only endpoints.
- Sampling thresholds: set cpu_queue_ms cutoff at 50ms vs 30ms? 50ms reduces noise but may miss early warning.
- KV warmth instrumentation overhead on private deployments; need compatibility check with on-prem logging stacks.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Implement kvcache.warmth_ratio derivation in runtime metrics exporter — owner: Mateo Alvarez — ETA: 2025-12-03.
- Add rollout_tag annotation to trace header and SDKs — owner: Priya Nair — ETA: 2025-12-10.
- Create operator quickcard dashboard skeleton with pre-aggregates — owner: Hannah Liu — ETA: 2025-12-17.
- Kick off probe experiment (JIRA-ENG-2581) — owner: Jordan Blake — ETA: 2025-12-01.

Notes to reviewers:
- Please call out any metric we've omitted that you rely on during triage. Trying to keep the live quickcard under 6 panels.
- Feedback needed on sampling policy thresholds and acceptable trace retention limits for the reservoir.

Appendix: quick examples
- Example metric contract snippet (text):
  name: kvcache.warmth_ratio
  description: fraction of requests that hit the prefix/kv cache for the given model_version and tenant in the window
  unit: ratio (0..1)
  labels: [model_version, tenant_id (rollup only), region]
  expected_baseline: 0.72 +/- 0.08
  alerting: fire if rolling10m < 0.5 and requests.count>1000

- Trace search example query (for operator quicklink):
  "cpu_queue_ms:>50 AND model_version:canary-2026-01 AND kv_hit:false"

Rough meeting log (session 2):
- 2026-01-12 10:00 — Reviewed last canary traces + agreed on metric shortlist.
- 2026-01-12 10:30 — Decided on severity-weighted sampling approach.
- 2026-01-15 — Followed up on prototype probe design and data retention sketch.

End of doc.
